mechanism_narrative: The continued decline in WORKPLACES from -9.4 to -8.6 and the persistently low TRANSIT level imply a durable commuting recovery. That should lift discretionary footfall into retail and recreation over the next four weeks as weekday trips bundle shopping and leisure with work travel.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay flat or fall again while RETAIL_REC remains below the prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in PARKS from 26.1 to 4.6 signals a substitution away from outdoor leisure. Within one to two weeks, those trips should reallocate to indoor retail and dining, raising RETAIL_REC relative to the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 10 and stays there for 2 consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: If PARKS remains below 10 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve within the next 14 days, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: When grocery-pharmacy mobility stays elevated while residential time is also elevated, routine errand traffic generates spillovers into nearby retail. Because GROCERY_PHARM is still rising and RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline, RETAIL_REC should edge up over four weeks if these two series move together.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both stay elevated but RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four-week mean, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: If transit mobility falls further below its already depressed level, access friction to shopping corridors increases and retail visits should weaken within one week. This is a direct transport-capacity channel and should show up fastest when TRANSIT drops below the current trough.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week from the current level
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls by more than 3 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not decline within the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The large week-to-week swing in PARKS indicates weather-sensitive leisure substitution. In a cooler or wetter regime, a sustained park pullback should redirect outing demand toward indoor retail over the next two to four weeks, increasing RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS drops by at least 10 points from a prior weekly high
failure_condition: If PARKS drops sharply again but RETAIL_REC does not exceed the last 4-week average within 28 days, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL time stays above baseline and WORKPLACES remain suppressed, households consolidate errands into fewer outside trips. That consolidation should support retail and recreation spending in the next two weeks, especially if the current pattern persists rather than reversing.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and WORKPLACES stay below baseline but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in GROCERY_PHARM alongside falling PARKS indicates consumers are shifting from leisure outings to necessity-driven trips. Under restriction-driven behavior, that mix usually precedes weaker discretionary retail visits over the following month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises for 2 consecutive weeks while PARKS falls for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising and PARKS keeps falling but RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior 4 weeks, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of weak TRANSIT, weak WORKPLACES, and only modestly positive RESIDENTIAL suggests subdued daily circulation rather than a broad recovery in outside activity. If this low-mobility regime persists, RETAIL_REC should remain below the previous 4-week average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated but RETAIL_REC rises above the prior 4-week mean, this hypothesis is rejected.
